title: Model consistency advisory and tenant self-audit kit — ambiguous-output patterns
summary: Customers may observe ambiguous or semantically inconsistent outputs for requests served between 2026-06-03 01:00 UTC and 2026-06-03 08:40 UTC. This advisory explains what we saw, what we fixed, and gives a compact self-audit checklist tenants can run to verify whether they were affected and to collect evidence for support requests.
customer_impact: Intermittent variations in returned text where paraphrases or small factual shifts appeared across otherwise identical requests. Not a full outage; affected customers may see different phrasing, altered punctuation that changes meaning, or rare hallucinations in reply fields. No data loss reported. A subset of traffic routed through EU compute experienced the highest rate of variance.
root_cause_summary: During a rolling kernel and optimized-quantization patch to improve cost-per-token we introduced a subtle change in layer-fusion ordering for specific model builds. On GPUs with older cu* drivers this changed numeric rounding in KV-cache updates for mid-sequence tokens, which manifested as semantic parity drift for a measurable fraction of requests. The change only affected one model family variant and a limited hardware subset during the rollout window.
incident_timeline:
2026-06-03 00:50 UTC: rollout of quantization kernel patch began to a single pool.
2026-06-03 01:30 UTC: internal anomaly detection flagged elevated semantic-variance scores for model family M-alpha in EU region.
2026-06-03 02:10 UTC: on-call began investigation, reproduced variance in lab by replaying sampled traffic against patched runtime.
2026-06-03 03:05 UTC: rollback to previous kernel build initiated for impacted pools.
2026-06-03 04:00 UTC: traffic gradually transitioned back to baseline; variance rates declining.
2026-06-03 08:40 UTC: monitoring showed return to normal variance baselines; rollout halted pending deeper postmortem.
tenant_self_audit_steps:
1) Identify representative requests: pick 5-10 recent requests that you think produced ambiguous or shifted outputs (include timestamps and tenant request IDs).
2) Re-run these requests against the same pinned model version if you use model pins. If you did not pin a model, include original model name from response metadata.
3) Export two responder transcripts: the original response (copy from your logs) and a fresh call made now; compare differences in meaning, not just punctuation.
4) Run the quick parity check sample commands below (curl examples) to collect logs.
5) If you see meaningful semantic changes, gather: tenant_id, request_id, model_name, timestamp (UTC), region, and a short note describing the semantic difference. Attach these to a support ticket.

Quick parity check (example curl):
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"M-alpha","input":"<your-prompt>","stream":false}'
Run the same command three times and capture outputs; include the three outputs verbatim in your report.

Note: avoid sending PII; redact as necessary.
sample_payload_for_support:
Please include the following in any support ticket:
- tenant_id: (string)
- example_request_ids: [comma-separated request ids]
- timestamps_utc: [range or exact timestamps]
- model_name_and_revision: (e.g., M-alpha@2026-05-27-buildX)
- region: (e.g., eu-west-1)
- short_description_of_difference: (one sentence each)
- three raw responses from the quick parity check above
Linked logs (if available): request logs URL or exported JSON.
Example subject line: "Variance: M-alpha EU semantic drift 2026-06-03 — tenant 12345"
recommended_mitigations_for_customers: If you rely on strict semantic stability for production flows we recommend: 1) Pin to a known-good model revision (use model pinning in the API). 2) Enable conservative mode for paraphrase-sensitive routes (adjust sampling/temp params: temperature=0.0, top_p=0.0). 3) Temporarily route critical calls to Dedicated or Private deployments if you have them and require absolute determinism. 4) Run the self-audit steps and open a support ticket if you find evidence — we can provide replay evidence or offer targeted rollbacks for enterprise tenants.
operator_actions_taken:
- Immediate rollback of the quantization kernel patch for affected pools.
- Scoped mitigation: we added a canary gate and expanded unit tests for KV-cache numeric stability.
- Expanded post-deploy validation: new binary-level parity checks and synthetic semantic test-suite run during rollouts.
- Customer outreach: this advisory and targeted notifications for customers with high variance scores.
next_steps_and_timeline:
- Short term (1–3 days): complete the postmortem with a full root-cause write-up and publish the technical appendix.
- Medium term (2–6 weeks): ship improved numerical guards and add per-model hardware compatibility matrix to rollout tooling.
- Long term (3+ months): integrate semantic-parity regression checks into CI for all model families and provide a customer-facing model-change calendar for major runtime changes.
contact: For support: support@redwood.ai with subject prefix 'Variance incident 2026-06-03'. For enterprise customers: your Customer Success Manager (CC list: Miguel Santos, Aisha Patel). Operational slack channel: #cust-ops-variance. For urgent escalations call SRE pager (via on-call) or open an incident in Jira: INF-4921.
operator_notes: Avoid instructing customers to reprocess large historical corpora without support — if a tenant requests mass-replay we will coordinate a replay plan to avoid double-charging and to preserve ordering semantics. We will not issue automatic credits; credits will be considered per-tenant after verification.
